accuracy.evidence: Checked against Common Core W.3.3 (establish a situation; dialogue and descriptions of actions, thoughts and feelings; temporal words and phrases to signal event order; a sense of closure), W.4.3d (concrete words and sensory details), W.5.3b (pacing) and the National Curriculum in England Years 5-6 (integrate dialogue to convey character and advance the action; cohesion through adverbials of time). Scene and summary are used in the standard craft sense (moment-by-moment telling versus compressed time), and every lab verdict matches it: the freeze (problem) and the dive (turning point) are scenes, the other three events are summaries.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented weaknesses in 7-11 narrative writing: equal detail for every event (Read it with all scenes says 'nothing stands out', all summary says 'reads like a list'), 'and then' chains (Then is refused with 'does not tell the reader how much time passed'), small-talk dialogue (hellos and weather chat are cut), naming a feeling instead of showing it (the Tell card 'Zara was very scared' is refused), 'Suddenly' for unsurprising events, and dream or new-problem endings.

lab_distinct.evidence: The mechanism is pacing: bars that widen into scenes or shrink into summaries and are judged against where the problem and turning point are, a four-line slow-motion builder that refuses two lines of one kind in a row and needs three kinds, dialogue lines tagged by job, gap-by-gap time adverbials and endings tested against the stated problem. flagmentor sorts show/tell and setting mood, flagplot builds a story mountain and flagtale orders picture cards for 5-7s; none paces scenes. The 30% shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers the rule by trying: making everything a scene or nothing a scene is rejected with a reason tied to the specific event, adding two actions in a row is blocked, filler chat appears struck out with a scissors icon, a wrong link is outlined in red with its reason, and an ending only marks the arc 'solved' when it answers the problem. Step text confirms each idea only after the task is complete.

predictions.evidence: Two locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'The start, so the reader knows everything' gets the most words (a common habit of long openings) is disproved when the pacing check accepts scenes only at the freeze and the dive; 'Yes, it sounds real' for hellos and how-are-yous is disproved when the lab cuts every small-talk line.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with twelve tagged messages: a scene spent on putting on shoes or the walk, hellos and weather chat kept, Suddenly for a bus ride, Then with no time span, dream and new-problem endings, five actions in a row, naming the feeling, 'summaries are lazy' and 'readers want every detail'.

readability.evidence: Kid text reads at FK about 2 with short sentences built around Zara's dive and Tom's dog; adult text reads at FK about 8.4 and uses the exact terms narrative, pacing, scene, summary, dialogue, sensory details, temporal words and phrases, adverbials of time, cohesion and closure. Canvas labels are one to six words and the lab text is plain.

no_filler.evidence: Passed the filler patterns and the 12% duplicate gate against every lesson, including Planning Narratives, Plot Structure and Character Development and Simple stories with a beginning and an ending. Each kid paragraph adds new tools (the problem, pacing, the slow-motion mix, then dialogue with a job, time phrases and endings); adult paragraphs give the standards, the scene/summary idea, common mistakes and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android light and iPhone 13 dark screenshots of all six steps: five pacing bars with short labels, the four slow-motion lines with kind chips, the dialogue script, the link chain with its gaps and the ending arc all fit with nothing clipped; the long line buttons wrap within the panel. phone_sweep found no overflow or clipped text.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: every task completes with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, the challenge shows, axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in light and dark themes, no console errors. Every canvas tap has a button (one per event plus Read it, one per line, one per time phrase, one per ending) with an aria-label that names the event and its state, and the canvas aria-label reports each result.
